visual.general_description: Schematic diagram of the carnitine shuttle enzymes CPT1, CACT, CPT2 and CAT across the outer and inner mitochondrial membranes.
visual.detailed_description: White-background cell-biology schematic with three red section labels down the left edge: "Cytosol" at the top, "Intermembrane space" in the middle and "Mitochondrial matrix" at the bottom. Two horizontal lipid bilayers are drawn: the upper one is labelled "Outer mitochondrial membrane" and has a yellow rounded enzyme shape labelled "CPT1" embedded in it; the lower one is labelled "Inner mitochondrial membrane" and holds a large green shape labelled "CPT2" in the centre and two red shapes labelled "CACT", one on each side of it. At the top, black text "Long-chain fatty acids" has a thick downward arrow to "Acyl-CoA", with a "CoA" label and a small curved arrow joining the arrow. Metabolite labels "Carnitine" and "Acetyl-Carnitine" are printed with the word "Carnitine" in blue and the prefix in black. Vertical thin arrows connect these labels between the cytosol, intermembrane space and matrix columns: one column of arrows points downward on the left and two columns of arrows point upward on the right. In the matrix, curved arrows from the CPT2 shape lead to "Acyl-CoA" and "Carnitine", with a "CoA" label; "Acyl-CoA" is followed by small downward arrows through "β-oxidation" to "Acetyl-CoA", then a "CoA" arrow and a dashed circular "TCA Cycle" symbol. A grey-blue shape labelled "CAT" sits beside labels "Acetyl-CoA", "CoA" and "Acetyl-Carnitine" at the lower right.
